## Verdict
- Answer: "Tariffs" dominates coverage: 479,208 articles, 88.4% of the three-term total of 541,937 [c1]. "Trade war" has 61,081 (11.3%) and "stock market crash" has 1,648 (0.3%) [c1]. Tariffs is about 291 times the volume of "stock market crash" (computed from [c1]).
- Decision: Treat "tariffs" as the main news topic when allocating monitoring effort. Treat "trade war" as a secondary framing and "stock market crash" as a small, spike-driven niche.
- Confidence: medium - the counts are measured, but they come from a single query and the tone measure is a classifier whose definition is not documented. Common-word and overlap effects were not checked.
- What would change it: A de-duplicated, per-source breakdown showing that the "tariffs" count is inflated by non-news or boilerplate uses.

## What the data shows
Window: 2024-06-01 to 2026-05-31 (end exclusive 2026-06-01), monthly, 24 months [c1].

| Term | Articles | Share | Critical | Critical % (computed) | Direction | Growth | Tone ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tariffs | 479,208 [c1] | 88.4% [c1] | 365,884 [c1] | 76.4% | rising [c1] | 2.18 [c1] | 2.9 [c1] |
| trade war | 61,081 [c1] | 11.3% [c1] | 48,061 [c1] | 78.7% | rising [c1] | 1.35 [c1] | 4.59 [c1] |
| stock market crash | 1,648 [c1] | 0.3% [c1] | 1,154 [c1] | 70.0% | flat [c1] | 0.92 [c1] | 4.23 [c1] |

- most_covered: tariffs [c1]. combined_articles: 541,937 [c1].
- Peak months: April 2025 for all three terms. Tariffs had 93,515 articles [c1], trade war 19,452 [c1], and stock market crash 329 [c1].
- April 2025 held about 19.5% of all "tariffs" articles in the window (93,515 / 479,208, computed from [c1]).
- Monthly "tariffs" coverage in May 2026 was 8,774 [c1], against 3,363 in June 2024 [c1]. That is roughly 2.6 times the start, but far below the April 2025 peak.
- Tone: the tool reports a "tone_ratio" and a "critical" count, but I have no definition of how it computes them. My reading is that the tone ratio is the ratio of negative to positive articles. I checked this against the monthly rows and it does not hold exactly: for tariffs, summed negatives over positives is not obviously 2.9. Treat the ratio as a tool-defined index and do not interpret it beyond that. "Critical" is the tool's classification and is shown as a share of each term's articles.
- The tool's "vs_baseline" values are 5.0 for tariffs, 7.91 for trade war, and 7.29 for stock market crash [c1]. The baseline is not defined in the output, so I do not interpret them.

## Trend

(The chart shows a subset of months for readability; the full series is in the CSV.)

Quantified change:
- Tariffs rose from 3,363 in June 2024 to a 93,515 peak in April 2025 [c1], which is 27.8 times (computed). By May 2026 it had fallen back to 8,774 [c1], which is 9.4% of the peak (computed).

The monthly stock market crash share is noisy because of small counts; for example, December 2025 was 34.6% on 26 articles [c1].

## Method and limits
